title: Ultrasound-guided lymph node fine-needle aspiration for evaluating post-vaccination germinal center responses
author: Scholte, Leggat, et al.

steps.title: Prepare R10 culture media
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet (BSC‑2) thaw RPMI‑1640, L‑glutamine (200 mM), Antibiotic/Antimycotic, 1 M HEPES, and heat‑inactivated FBS; combine 100 mL RPMI‑1640, 1.1 mL Antibiotic/Antimycotic, 1.1 mL 1 M HEPES, 1.1 mL 200 mM L‑glutamine, and 11 mL HI‑FBS; invert gently ~1 min, aliquot into sterile containers, label, and store at 2–8 °C (stable ≤1 week).

substeps.instruction: Prepare BSC‑2 and place all reagents inside.
Allow frozen reagents to thaw under aseptic conditions.
Open containers only inside the BSC‑2.
Transfer the specified volumes into a sterile container.
Close, invert gently for ~1 min to mix.
Aliquot 100 mL portions, label “R10 Media”, expiration, storage.
Store at 2–8 °C; discard if color changes pink→yellow (pH shift).
CRITICAL: Do not thaw HI‑FBS >37 °C; aliquot and store at –20 °C if not used immediately; never refreeze thawed aliquots.

steps.title: Prepare cell freezing media (CFM)
steps.instruction: In a BSC‑2, thaw sterile FBS (2–8 °C overnight or 37 °C water bath) and DMSO; for each 90 mL FBS add 10 mL DMSO, mix, aliquot into single‑use tubes, label “CFM”, and store at –20 °C (stable 1 yr); thawed CFM may be kept 2–8 °C ≤12 h.

substeps.instruction: Prepare BSC‑2.
Thaw FBS in refrigerator (preferred) or 37 °C water bath.
Open FBS and DMSO aseptically.
Mix 90 mL FBS with 10 mL DMSO (exothermic).
Aliquot into single‑use tubes, label, store at –20 °C.
CRITICAL: Chill CFM at 2–8 °C ≥30 min (or on ice ≥15 min) before use.

steps.title: Prepare 1× RBC lysis buffer
steps.instruction: In a BSC‑2, dilute 10× RBC lysis buffer 1:10 with UltraPure DNase/RNase‑Free distilled water (1 mL concentrate + 9 mL water); label “1× RBC lysis buffer”, store at 2–8 °C (stable 1 working day).

substeps.instruction: Prepare BSC‑2.
Place 10× RBC lysis buffer and water bottles in BSC‑2.
Open both containers aseptically.
For each 1 mL 10× buffer add 9 mL water.
Label container with name, expiration, storage.
Store at 2–8 °C; use within one working day.

steps.title: Verify participant and assemble needles
steps.instruction: Confirm participant ID, consent, vaccine arm, and pregnancy test (if applicable); prepare four sterile 22–23 G lumbar puncture needles attached to 5–10 mL syringes, place on a sterile drape‑covered tray.

substeps.instruction: Check name, study ID, and signed consent.
Identify arm that received vaccine; FNA will be performed on same side.
If participant is a female of child‑bearing potential, confirm same‑day negative pregnancy test; abort if positive.
Prepare four sterile 22–23 G lumbar puncture needles.
Attach each needle to a 5–10 mL sterile syringe.
Place needles on a movable tray covered with a sterile drape.
CRITICAL: Maintain sterile technique throughout needle preparation.

steps.title: Prepare transport tubes with R10 media
steps.instruction: In an insulated bio‑transport container, place two 50 mL conical tubes (labeled with participant ID) on wet ice: one tube contains 10 mL R10 media (“For Collection”), the other 50 mL R10 media (“For Flushing”).

substeps.instruction: Put two 50 mL conical tubes inside a Saf‑TPak container filled with wet ice.
Add 10 mL R10 media to the first tube; label “For Collection”.
Add 50 mL R10 media to the second tube; label “For Flushing”.

steps.title: Ultrasound‑guided lymph node aspiration
steps.instruction: Position participant supine with the target arm extended, external rotation, elbow flexed; disinfect axilla, cover with sterile drape, apply local 1 % lidocaine (2–4 mL), locate a ≥0.7 cm LN by high‑frequency US (use color Doppler to avoid vessels), then perform up to four needle passes with negative pressure (2–3 mL pull) and “to‑and‑fro” motion, flushing each needle three times with R10 media into the “For Collection” tube.

substeps.instruction: Place participant supine; raise target arm above head, rest on pillow.
Scan axilla with high‑frequency US; identify LN ≥0.7 cm in three planes.
Use color Doppler to confirm normal hilum vascularity and avoid vessels.
Cover chest distal to axilla with sterile drape; place sterile US probe cover.
Swab axilla generously with chlorhexidine, betadine, or equivalent; verify no allergy.
Administer 2–4 mL 1 % lidocaine into skin/subcutaneous tissue over LN.
Insert a prepared 22–23 G needle‑syringe under real‑time US guidance.
When needle tip is visualized inside LN, withdraw plunger to 2–3 mL mark to create negative pressure.
Perform gentle “to‑and‑fro” motion, mild rotations within cortex; repeat briskly to collect material.
Maintain negative pressure while withdrawing needle; most aspirate remains in needle hub.
Submerge needle tip in the “For Collection” 50 mL tube; expel all contents into media.
Detach needle from syringe; keep needle in the same tube.
Draw 2–3 mL R10 media from the “For Flushing” tube into the empty syringe.
Re‑attach syringe to needle and flush media into the “For Collection” tube.
Repeat the flush (steps above) two more times for a total of three flushes per pass.
Discard the used needle and syringe in a biohazard sharps container.
Repeat steps from insertion to three flushes for up to four passes (use a new needle/syringe each pass).
CRITICAL: Use a new sterile needle/syringe for each pass; ensure three flushes per pass.

steps.title: Finalize sample collection and transport
steps.instruction: Cap both conical tubes, place them on wet ice in a screw‑top cylindrical specimen container, then into an insulated bio‑transport container for delivery to the processing lab; clean ultrasound gel, apply gauze pressure, and cover puncture site with adhesive bandage.

substeps.instruction: Replace screw caps on “For Collection” and “For Flushing” tubes.
Place capped tubes on wet ice inside a screw‑top cylindrical specimen container.
Put the specimen container into an insulated bio‑transport container and transport on ice to the processing laboratory.
Wipe residual ultrasound gel from participant’s skin.
Apply gauze pressure to any bleeding puncture sites until hemostasis.
Apply an adhesive bandage over each puncture site.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash aspirate cells
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool a centrifuge to 4 °C (2–8 °C acceptable); spin the “For Collection” tube at 325 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant down to ~10 mL with a serological pipette, then remove remaining supernatant with a 1000 µL pipette, resuspend pellet in 1 mL cold 1× PBS, bring volume to 50 mL with cold PBS, and repeat centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Set centrifuge to 4 °C (or 2–8 °C).
Centrifuge the “For Collection” tube at 325 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
After spin, locate small red pellet; aspirate supernatant down to ~10 mL using a serological pipette (avoid vacuum‑induced loss).
Aspirate remaining supernatant with a 1000 µL single‑channel pipette without disturbing pellet.
Resuspend pellet gently in 1 mL cold 1× sterile PBS (2–8 °C).
Add cold PBS to bring total volume to 50 mL; wash cells.
Centrifuge again at 325 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant as before; if pellet is not visible, assume it is present and proceed.

steps.title: Perform red blood cell lysis
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 × volume cold 1× RBC lysis buffer (e.g., 5 mL for ~500 µL pellet), incubate 4 min at ambient temperature with gentle rotation, bring volume to 35 mL with cold PBS, centrifuge 325 × g 10 min at 4 °C; repeat lysis once if pellet remains reddish; if still no visible pellet after second lysis, continue processing.

substeps.instruction: Add cold 1× RBC lysis buffer at 10 × pellet volume (example: 5 mL for ~0.5 mL pellet).
Incubate 4 min at room temperature, gently rotating.
Add cold PBS to bring total volume to 35 mL.
Centrifuge at 325 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
If pellet still appears red, aspirate supernatant and repeat lysis (steps above).
If after second lysis pellet is still not visualized, proceed to next step assuming cells are present.

steps.title: Count cells using viability dye
steps.instruction: Add 180 µL cold 1× PBS to a 0.6 mL microcentrifuge tube, add 20 µL cell suspension for a 1:10 dilution, mix; add 20 µL acridine orange/propidium iodide (AOPI) to a new tube, add 20 µL diluted cells for a final 1:20 dilution, mix, load 20 µL onto a labeled Cellometer slide, and run the Cellometer Auto 2000 (low RBC assay) with dilution factor set to 20; after counting, bring total volume to 35 mL with cold PBS and centrifuge 10 min at 325 × g, 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 180 µL cold 1× PBS to a 0.6 mL tube.
Transfer 20 µL cell suspension; mix for 1:10 dilution.
In a second 0.6 mL tube, add 20 µL AOPI dye.
Add 20 µL of the 1:10 diluted cells to the AOPI tube (final 1:20).
Mix thoroughly.
Transfer 20 µL of the GCC/AOPI mix to one side of a labeled Cellometer slide.
Run the Cellometer Auto 2000 using the “Immune cells, low RBC” assay, set dilution factor to 20.
CRITICAL: Use automated counter for rapid, accurate counts (range 1 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁷ cells/mL).
After counting, adjust total volume to 35 mL with cold PBS.
Centrifuge 10 min at 325 × g, 4 °C.
Aspirate supernatant as previously described; if pellet not visible, proceed to cryopreservation.

steps.title: Aliquot cells and cryopreserve
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final cell pellet in chilled CFM to achieve ~4 000 cells/µL (4 × 10⁶ cells/mL) or as required; dispense 1 mL aliquots into cryovials (label volume and total cell number; if <1 mL, label as “partial”), place vials in a controlled‑rate freezing container for 4–96 h at –80 °C, then transfer to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage (up to indefinite).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in enough chilled CFM to reach 4 000 cells/µL (or study‑specified concentration).
If total volume is between 0.5–1 mL, note as a “partial” aliquot and record exact volume and cell count on the label.
If fewer than 500 µL are needed, resuspend in 500 µL CFM and label accordingly.
Transfer 1 mL (or partial volume) into each cryovial.
Write volume and total cell number on vial label with permanent marker or printed cryolabel.
Place filled vials into a controlled‑rate freezing container.
Freeze at –80 °C for a minimum of 4 h and maximum of 96 h.
After freezing, move vials to cryoboxes and store at –80 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Transfer vials to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage (indefinite).
PAUSE POINT: Samples may remain cryopreserved indefinitely in LN₂.
